source.check: returned without a contest: 'Downpatrick Rural Council will show only one change' (Kilmore) and 'There will be no contests' (Belfast News-Letter, 7 May 1936, p. 15); the council recorded his resignation of 'his membership for the Castlewellan rural division' and co-opted Joseph M'Sherry in his place, July 1936 (Belfast News-Letter, 9 July 1936, p. 5; Irish Independent, 18 July 1936, p. 12); he sat on the previous council (Dromore Leader, 2 September 1933) (round 2, 7 Nov 2026)

note: Triennial election of the Downpatrick rural district council, 1936; polling day for Co. Down, Thursday 4 June 1936. There were no contests and only one change, at Kilmore (Belfast News-Letter, 7 May 1936, p. 15). The unchanged divisions are not named. Four more divisions (Dunmore, Killinchy, Killyleagh Rural, Strangford) are recorded from the report of the new council's annual meeting on 10 June 1936, each with its division from the 1930 return, and Castlewellan Rural from the report of its member's resignation in July 1936, when Joseph M'Sherry was co-opted in his place (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). The Castlewellan Rural member, Felix M'Kenna, sat on the previous council and, the 1936 nominations making only one change (Kilmore), was returned again; he resigned within weeks, and the council co-opted Joseph M'Sherry in July 1936 (a co-option, not an election). Returned unopposed.
